The continuous operation of the service, the repeated administration of identity and reputation and the institutional presence of the game as a platform of participation generate abundant and heterogeneous empirical material, with user statements, records of conflicts and technical-normative documentation circulating in multiple layers.<1>p. 59-60</1>

It is an environment with a strong presence in the Brazilian market, a sophisticated business model in terms of monetization of digital goods and wide availability of public documentary material and public statements by consumer users.<1>p. 38</1>

The case plays a supporting role, not a leading one, and appears in vignettes when a category needs to be stabilized or when it must be shown how the formal rule becomes execution practice. This use is controlled by the distinction among three layers of normativity. The declared one lies in the terms, policies and announcements. The one in operation lies in the technical architecture, the interface flows and the concrete forms of enforcement and sanction, and it is there that the promise takes shape and that much of the informational asymmetry is produced.
In the work as a whole, the selected ecosystem plays a supporting role, not a leading one.<1>p. 58</1>

Recourse to the case is delimited and instrumental, because it serves to anchor inferences and to make concrete certain mechanisms whose formulation, on the abstract level, might sound excessively generic. For this reason, references to the ecosystem will be used as vignettes and points of support, triggered only when necessary to stabilize the meaning of a category, illustrate a typical governance arrangement or show the way a formal rule is converted into execution practice.<1>p. 57</1>

There is, in the first place, a declared normativity, which presents itself in the form of terms, policies, rules and institutional announcements, through which the platform describes the service, defines conditions of access, establishes rights and duties and announces, when it wishes, the limits of the promised experience.<1>p. 58</1>

There is, in the second place, a normativity in operation, which is not reduced to the formal text and manifests itself in the technical architecture, in the interface flows, in the execution routines, in the mechanisms of modulation of the experience and in the concrete forms of enforcement and sanction. This layer is decisive, because it is there that the contractual promise takes shape and it is also there that a relevant part of the informational asymmetry typical of continuous digital consumption is produced.<1>p. 58</1>

The disputed one arises when the first two come into friction, because execution reveals what the text did not clarify, because the text serves as an alibi or because unilateral change shifts the balance without the consumer knowing what was altered. Separating them prevents confusing statement with execution, promise with delivery and controversy with mechanism. The case has limits. The design focuses on this ecosystem, in the computer and mobile versions, the latter called Wild Rift, under a defined time frame and with public sources, and this option does not map variations by platform, national market or technological generation, nor does it authorize statistical inference. The reflection, therefore, is not about League of Legends as an isolated cultural object, but about the regime of the immaterial object of consumption contained in it.

There is, further, a disputed normativity, which emerges when the two previous layers come into friction, whether because execution reveals consequences that the text did not clarify, whether because the text functions as an alibi for practices perceived as abusive, or whether because unilateral changes shift the balance of the service without the consumer being able to recognize, with precision, what was altered and with what effects.<1>p. 58</1>

Delimiting these arenas is not a classificatory whim, but a way of preventing the analysis from confusing statement with execution, promise with delivery or controversy with mechanism, as well as ensuring that each argumentative step rests on the appropriate layer of the phenomenon examined.<1>p. 58</1>

The methodological design focuses on a paradigmatic case, the Riot Games ecosystem with League of Legends, in its desktop and mobile (“Wild Rift”) versions, under a defined time frame and relying on public and documentary sources, so as to compose a verifiable corpus. This option limits the mapping of variations by type of platform, by national market and by technological generation, and is not oriented to producing statistical inferences from a representative sample.<1>p. 78-79</1>

The work's potential for generalization derives, first, from what the instrumental empirical laboratory makes observable, not from what would be “typical” or “individual” about the case, producing analytical generalization through mechanisms and relevant frictions. For this reason, this work does not propose a reflection on League of Legends as an isolated cultural object, but on the regime of the immaterial object of consumption contained in it and on the techniques of private governance employed by the continuous digital services that sustain it, reconstructed with the support of an ecosystem that clearly makes explicit dependence, modulation of access, internal sanctions, an economy of virtual items and semiotic management of enjoyment.<1>p. 79</1>
What weight does each type of information carry?

Each piece of information has a graduated weight. General knowledge widespread in the sector serves only to situate the reader, without proving a specific occurrence. Auxiliary technical-operational descriptions name structures and explain the vocabulary of the field. Normatively relevant statements, such as promises, powers of modulation, sanction criteria, contestation procedures and restoration parameters, require, when they serve as a premise of legal qualification, traceable and attributable sources, with priority for the supplier's primary documentation.

To preserve proportionality between documentation effort and argumentative weight, a distinction is adopted among three layers of information mobilized throughout the work. The first comprises elements of general knowledge widely spread in the sector, used only to situate the reader and make the logic of continuous digital services intelligible, without claiming to prove a specific occurrence.<1>p. 60</1>

The second comprises auxiliary technical-operational descriptions, used to name internal structures and understand the vocabulary of the field, with subsidiary support in collaborative repositories when indispensable.<1>p. 60</1>

The third comprises normatively relevant statements, such as institutional promises, powers of modulation, sanction criteria, contestation procedures and restoration parameters, which are supported, whenever mobilized as a premise of legal qualification, by traceable and attributable sources, with priority for the supplier's primary documentation and verifiable public records.<1>p. 60</1>

With Umberto Eco, the sources, which make up the observed institutional world or the law in force, such as terms of use, policies, announcements, interface records, legal documents and court decisions, are kept separate from the critical literature that comments on them. The separation prevents commentary from being taken as evidence of what the platform declared or did, and indirect reading from replacing primary material when the argument depends on imputation. Dogmatic analysis is not an empirical source, and functions as a lens that organizes what counts as evidence, and the rule is triangulation, not exhaustiveness.

Sources are considered to be the materials that directly make up the observed institutional world or the law in force that bears on it, such as terms of use, internal policies, supplier announcements, interface records, legal documents and accessible court decisions. Critical literature is considered to be the set of texts that comment on, interpret, systematize or dispute these materials, such as doctrine, academic articles and third-party analyses. The distinction is not formalism, since it prevents commentary from being treated as evidence of what the platform declared or did, and prevents, moreover, indirect reading from replacing contact with primary material when the argument depends on dogmatic imputation.<1>p. 50</1>

Dogmatic and bibliographic analysis, in turn, is not treated as an “empirical source”, but as a lens of interpretation that organizes what counts as evidence, what counts as a promise and what counts as relevant loss in the regime of the Immaterial Object of Consumption.<1>p. 61</1>
The general rule is to work by triangulation and sufficiency of the core of evidence pertinent to the argument, instead of pursuing exhaustiveness or representativeness.<1>p. 60</1>

These rules are tied to imputation, and so they also serve those who will litigate. Legal imputation remains conditioned on traceable elements when the argument depends on it, and, when the argument requires institutional attribution, such as an internal rule, a sanction criterion or a binding promise, support falls on attributable sources, with public narratives only as a starting point. For public content that may change, traceability is ensured by the minimum record of the item identifier, the address and the date of access. The chapter on proof carries this discipline into the lawsuit.

When the text resorts to descriptions of functioning widely spread in the sector, they operate as contextualization and not as proof of a specific occurrence, legal imputation remaining conditioned on traceable elements when the argument depends on it.<1>p. 59</1>

When, however, the argument depends on specific institutional attribution, such as the content of an internal rule, a sanction criterion, a binding promise or a restoration procedure, support falls on traceable and attributable sources, with public narratives used only as a starting point for locating verifiable elements.<1>p. 67</1>

In the case of public content subject to alteration, traceability is ensured by a minimum record of the item identifier, the source address and the date of access, without claiming to constitute an exhaustive repository of full captures.<1>p. 61</1>
What can each source prove, and what can it not?

Situated institutional observation makes the norm in operation visible. It is neither ethnography nor personal account as proof, but observation of the platform as a functioning institution, in which interface, flows and communications are institutional texts that distribute understanding unequally. System messages, warnings, notifications and mechanisms of restriction, sanction and contestation count as primary evidence when described in a traceable way. The technique describes patterns and mechanisms, without measuring statistical prevalence and without inferring the supplier's psychological intentions.

This is neither community ethnography nor an account of personal experience as proof. The procedure is employed to observe the platform as a functioning institution, that is, the mechanisms through which the offer is organized, the experience is conducted and the performance of the bond takes place through technical artifacts, interface flows and instruments of sanction.<1>p. 62</1>

Interface, flows and institutional communications are treated as institutional texts that organize meanings and distribute understanding unequally, guiding promises, expectations and modes of delivery. The cut falls on institutionally relevant elements observable in enjoyment, such as access and configuration flows, system messages, warnings and notifications, as well as mechanisms of restriction, sanction and contestation presented to the user, mobilized selectively when necessary to stabilize the description of the mechanism discussed.<1>p. 62</1>

The elements observed are treated as primary evidence when they can be described in a traceable way, preserving, where pertinent, the minimum context of their occurrence and the elements necessary to allow verification of what was described.<1>p. 62</1>

The reach of the procedure is to describe verifiable institutional patterns and mechanisms, without claiming to measure the statistical prevalence of individual experiences nor to infer the supplier's psychological intentions.<1>p. 63</1>

Documentary analysis captures the declared norm, the repertoire of promises, duties, unilateral powers and procedures that the supplier presents as a condition of use, and these pieces take part in configuring the content of supply over time. Terms of use, licenses and penalty and conduct policies form the primary normative core, and help pages, frequently asked questions and announcements have a complementary status, without replacing the core when formal powers, sanctions or risk are discussed. Documents do not prove, by themselves, the everyday application of the rules.

The set of documents actually mobilized in the text is selected for pertinence to the problem investigated and has the function of capturing the declared norm of the ecosystem, that is, the repertoire of promises, duties, unilateral powers and execution procedures presented as a condition of access and use. In platform-governed objects, such pieces do not operate as simple informational accessories, since they take part in configuring the content of supply over time and delimit, explicitly or implicitly, the range of admitted modulations, the sanction regimes and the mechanisms of contestation and restoration.<1>p. 63-64</1>

Terms of use, licenses and penalty and conduct policies are taken as the primary normative core of the governance regime, because they structure powers, duties and consequences. Support materials, help pages and official announcements are mobilized with a complementary status, apt to evidence public promises, declared procedures and justifications offered to the user, without replacing the normative core when the analysis depends on definitions of formal powers, sanction regimes or risk allocation.<1>p. 65</1>

The reach of the procedure is to delimit, with traceability, the declared institutional design of the ecosystem, without claiming that documents, by themselves, prove the concrete form of everyday application of the rules.<1>p. 66</1>

Public statements by users, in videos and on complaint platforms, are a symptomatic record of recurring frictions, useful for mapping conflicts and vocabularies and for guiding triangulation with the declared norm and the norm in operation. They do not prove institutional conduct nor establish, by themselves, internal policies, decision criteria or obligations assumed. Forums such as Reddit do not serve to infer representativeness or prevalence, and collaborative repositories such as Fandom serve only to name categories and describe mechanics.
Narratives of experience and user interpretations do not operate as an autonomous evidentiary basis.<1>p. 62</1>
The survey of public user statements is part of the empirical collection with a delimited and subsidiary purpose, as a symptomatic record of recurring frictions in the ecosystem.<1>p. 66</1>

The selection of public statements focuses on two main arenas, chosen because they function as recurring channels for publicizing conflicts in the ecosystem: YouTube, as a space for accounts and controversies in audiovisual format, and structured complaint platforms that record consumer conflicts in the user's language under thematic classification.<1>p. 67</1>

This material is not mobilized as autonomous proof of the supplier's institutional conduct, nor as a substitute for official documents, interface records, lawsuits or decisions. It is used to map recurring frictions, identify relevant vocabularies and discursive patterns and guide triangulation with the declared norm and with the norm in operation, under minimum selection and recording criteria that allow external verification of the material actually cited.<1>p. 66</1>

Community and platform sources, such as forums, social networks, collaborative repositories and creator content, are treated with a delimited and subsidiary methodological function. They are not mobilized to establish, by themselves, the content of the supplier's internal policies, its decision criteria, its moderation procedures or the existence of obligations assumed, nor to assert the occurrence of disputed institutional practices.<1>p. 67</1>

For this reason, Reddit is mobilized in a referenced way, preferably from mentions and links contained in videos or in documents already included, avoiding endless drift of the field. Its use does not serve to infer the representativeness of opinions or the prevalence of events, but to locate chains, terms of reference and verifiable leads when the public environment of the ecosystem makes them relevant.<1>p. 69</1>

To enrich the technical-operational intelligibility of terms, internal structures and vocabulary of the field, and only as a complement to official sources, collaborative repositories such as Fandom are used subsidiarily. This material is used for the strict purpose of naming categories of the ecosystem, operationally describing mechanics and auxiliary reconstruction of basic relations between elements of the service when indispensable to translate the functioning into legally intelligible language.<1>p. 69</1>
How should the platform's terms of use and policies be read?

Terms of use and policies are not a static declaration of will, but pieces of a governance device that integrates rule, implementation and continuous execution, with the promise recalibrated by interface, rewards, scarcity and sanctions. The contract remains legally central, because licenses, delimitations of access, unilateral powers and modulation clauses are articulated in it. The reading links these pieces to the functioning of the service to make the case decidable.

The institutional reading of the contract, in this work, starts from the recognition that terms of use and internal policies do not operate as static instruments of declaration of will, but as pieces of a governance device that integrates rule, implementation and continuous execution. In platform-governed ecosystems, the relevant promise is not exhausted in the contractual text, because it is reiterated and recalibrated by interface, reward routines, scarcity regimes and private sanctions.<1>p. 70</1>

Even so, the contract remains legally central, since it is in it that licenses, delimitations of access, unilateral powers and modulation clauses that sustain the enclosure and administration of the bond are articulated. The procedure adopted consists of articulating the formal pieces with the evidence of institutional functioning in order to bring the case back to the categories of the regime of the Immaterial Object of Consumption and make it legally decidable.<1>p. 70</1>

The reading is not a full exegesis, but a directed extraction along four axes, the qualification of the object and of the performance, the powers of unilateral modification and their triggers, the justification and allocation of risk, and the promises of compensation, refund and restoration. It also looks for which sanctions and channels of contestation exist and which duties of information apply when there is alteration, punishment or restriction. In software, the period of technical validity, update cycles, discontinuation and support come in. The version in force is read, preserved in the state of capture, and the previous one only with a verifiable public record.

Instead of a full exegesis of each piece, a directed extraction of normatively relevant elements is carried out to reconstruct, over the course of the bond, (i) the modes of qualification of the object and of the performance, (ii) the powers of unilateral modification and their triggers, (iii) the forms of institutional justification and of risk allocation, and (iv) the promises of compensation, refund and restoration.<1>p. 64</1>

In this sense, the aim is to identify how the service is described and promised, how access is structured and conditioned, which limits of use are set, which rules of conduct organize belonging, which mechanisms of sanction and restriction are provided for, which channels of contestation and review are offered, which refund and restoration regimes are declared and which informational duties are provided for in situations of alteration, punishment or restriction.<1>p. 64-65</1>

In the case of a computer program, the documentary extraction will also be conducted in a directed way, seeking (i) references to the period of technical validity of the version marketed, update cycles, discontinuation milestones and conditions of withdrawal from circulation; and (ii) the design and effectiveness of the channels for support, maintenance and provision of complementary technical services.<1>p. 65</1>

The documents actually mobilized are collected and preserved in the state in which they appeared at the moment of capture, with a record of context and minimum traceability metadata, so as to allow reconstruction of what was declared in the version used.<1>p. 65</1>

The contractual analysis takes as reference, as a rule, the versions in force and accessible in the period when the writing was closed (March 2026), with occasional consideration of past alterations only when there is a verifiable public record and when this is necessary to qualify a legally relevant modulation of the bond.<1>p. 71</1>

The reading articulates three levels. The documentary-normative one shows how the platform qualifies the object, reserves powers and promises compensation. The technical-semiological one shows how interface, metrics, visibility and rewards convert signs into value and discipline. The public experiential one shows recurring frictions and perceptions of loss. Interfaces, statements and marketing are read through semiotic vulnerability, and contracts and court decisions through the IOC, abusive teleology, open auditability and functional value equivalence.

First, an internal documentary-normative level, made up of terms of use, policies and official support documents, in which one observes how the platform qualifies the object, defines licenses and enclosures, reserves unilateral powers and presents justifications and promises of compensation. Second, a technical-semiological level, in which one observes how interface, metrics, visibility regimes and reward systems convert signs into value and into everyday discipline, producing dependencies and operational expectations. Third, a public experiential level, derived from open statements, in which one observes recurring patterns of friction, perception of loss and invocation of institutional promises and procedures.<1>p. 71</1>

Public statements, observation of interfaces and marketing materials are read in light of semiotic vulnerability and of mechanisms of anticipation and guidance by signs, so as to make intelligible how belonging, reputation, time and recognition make up the promise and the value of what is acquired. Contractual documents and court decisions are read in light of the qualification of the IOC as an immaterial product in a consumer relationship, of abusive teleology as a criterion for controlling architecture and governance, and of the parameters of open auditability and functional value equivalence as keys for dealing with opacity and mutability without neutralizing protection.<1>p. 71</1>

The complexity of the contract is neither a moral defect nor a virtue, but a legal sign of a regime that concentrates decision-making power, disperses information and shifts the conflict to execution. Posner, Eggleston and Zeckhauser come in instrumentally, with a perspective that authorizes treating the form of the contract as an indication of the institutional environment in which it operates. For Macaulay, contracts often function as self-planning, activated only as a last resort, which recommends privileging the factual situation. None of this replaces the CDC, and control remains dogmatic and protective, with the contract read as a governance interface, and not as a complete photograph of the relationship.

In continuous digital services, complexity is not merely textual length. It is an indication of the distribution of normativity across layers, with reservations of power, sanction patterns and restoration mechanisms that come to be part of the very infrastructure of what is acquired.<1>p. 72</1>

Complexity, here, is not treated as a moral defect of the contract, nor as a virtue in itself. It is treated as a legal sign of a supply regime that concentrates decision-making power, disperses information, makes comparability difficult and shifts the conflict to the continuous performance of the bond.<1>p. 72</1>

In this frame, the reference to Posner, Eggleston and Zeckhauser is strictly instrumental. Their perspective authorizes treating the form of the contract as an indication of the institutional environment in which it raises interpretive questions about essential content, legitimate expectations and typical zones of abusiveness in standardized and unilaterally structured contracts <1>Zeckhauser</1><2>(Posner; Eggleston; Zeckhauser, 2000, p. 92)</2>.<3>p. 72</3>

Converging with this caution, Macaulay indicates that contracts, in various situations, operate less as an ordinary mechanism of conflict resolution and more as a tool of self-planning, whose activation tends to occur as ultima ratio <1>Macaulay</1><2>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 55)</2>. For interpretive purposes, this recommends privileging the factual situation and the conflict actually manifested, instead of presupposing that the text fully describes the relationship and its concrete expectations <3>Macaulay</3><4>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 61)</4>.<5>p. 73</5>

With the adoption of this perspective, contractual complexity functions as a script for qualifying the bond, guiding the identification of zones of informational asymmetry, of possible structural advantages and of external factors relevant to the practical functioning of the contract, above all when the logic of use of these instruments is unilaterally established by hegemonic actors <1>Zeckhauser</1><2>(Posner; Eggleston; Zeckhauser, 2000, p. 92)</2>. This key does not replace the dogmatic parameters of the Consumer Protection Code, but acts as a methodological bridge that authorizes describing the phenomenon with sufficient rigor to sustain the theoretical reconstruction and the dogmatic conversion of the regime. This caveat does not alter the parameter of control, which remains dogmatic and protective, but describes a practical condition of reading in contracts that function as a governance interface and not as a complete photograph of the relationship.<3>p. 72-73</3>
What is object and what is instrument?

Authors of political economy, sociology, philosophy and communication appear in several chapters under a precise condition. In platform economies, power tends to mask itself as technical administration, and the risk is letting the appearance of neutrality replace the analysis of how private decisions produce practical norms. The methodology takes itself as a position-taking and treats the regime of the service as a coupling of clauses, interface and institutional practices.

In platform economies, power tends to mask itself as technical administration while it concentrates knowledge, organizes attention and redefines the conditions of participation. The central methodological risk, in the face of this type of object, is to let the appearance of neutrality of the functioning replace the analysis of the way private decisions produce practical norms and distribute asymmetries.<1>p. 45</1>

The methodology represents a position taken in the face of the type of power observed in platform economies and, therefore, in the face of the type of temptation that such an object produces in the researcher. In environments in which private administration and management of conduct present themselves as technical neutrality, the central analytical risk is to naturalize decisions as if they were simple “functioning”, to reduce institutional choices to “operational details” and to attribute to the user, as autonomy, responses that have already been induced by design, communication and mechanisms of incentive, disincentive and sanction. The methodological design, therefore, assumes as a premise that the functioning regime of the service emerges from the coupling of clauses, interface and institutional practices, which prevents readings that artificially separate norm, technique and culture.<1>p. 45</1>

The distinction between object and instruments comes from Umberto Eco. The object is the regime of platform-governed enjoyment, with its mechanisms of promise, expectation, modulation and sanction, and it is a real phenomenon, not a book. The instruments are the conceptual keys that translate it into language apt for normative incidence, compatible with duties, limits and legal consequences. The references from other fields come in to identify mechanisms and discipline inferences, without exegesis of the works, which prevents both exegetical drift and the ornamental use of concepts.

The object consists of the regime of platform-governed enjoyment and its mechanisms of promise, expectation, modulation and sanction. The instruments are the conceptual keys used to qualify this regime in language apt for normative incidence, which makes it possible to convert phenomena of architecture, communication and technical execution into operational categories compatible with duties, limits and legal consequences.<1>p. 46</1>
“A thesis studies an object using certain instruments. Often the object is a book and the instruments are other books.<1>p. 46</1>

In other cases, on the contrary, the object is a real phenomenon; this is what happens with theses on internal migratory movements in present-day Italy, on the behavior of a group of disabled children or on the opinions of the public regarding a television program currently being broadcast.” <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 69)</2>.<3>p. 46</3>

In practical terms, references from political economy, sociology, philosophy, the anthropology of consumption and communication theory come in to guide the identification of relevant mechanisms and discipline inferences, without imposing an exegetical reconstruction of the works mobilized, so that the argument remains traceable back to traceable evidence and recognizable normative parameters <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 69-70)</2>. This distinction aims to prevent both exegetical drift and the merely ornamental use of concepts.<3>p. 46-47</3>

The non-exegetical approach is a conscious delimitation of focus, not a shortcut. When a concept reads an object different from the one in which it was born, what matters is what it makes visible, and genealogy only becomes a topic when necessary to prevent distortion. Eco gives the example of the American avant-garde of the 1950s that appropriated Zen, a case in which what matters is what it made of Zen, and not what Zen was at its origin. When a chapter turns to a philosopher or an economist, therefore, it does so to qualify the phenomenon, and the legal argument remains traceable back to evidence and to normative parameters.

In this key, the option for a non-exegetical approach does not operate as a shortcut, but as a conscious delimitation of focus. When a concept is mobilized as a tool to read an object distinct from the one in which it was formed, the interest lies in what it makes visible in the observed field and in the way it improves the legal intelligibility of the problem, without this imposing a philological reconstruction of the origin, internal debates and historical variants of the concept in its domain of birth, except when indispensable to avoid relevant distortion.<1>p. 47</1>

Eco offers an express formulation to justify cuts in which what is sought is not a full philological reconstruction of a thought at its origin, but the examination of uses and appropriations in another context, provided the objective is clearly delimited.<1>p. 47</1>
Suppose, however, that, when examining the critical literature, I became interested in the use that a certain American literary and artistic avant-garde made of Zen in the 1950s.<1>p. 47</1>

Assuming, of course, that I do not intend to show that the Californians misunderstood the original Zen, which would make comparison with the Japanese texts mandatory. But if I limit myself to presupposing that they were freely inspired by translations from the Japanese, what interests me is what they made of Zen and not what Zen was at its origin.” <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 70-71)</2>.<3>p. 47</3>

The roles are ranked. The instruments guide the gaze, the sources support what is asserted, and the critical literature qualifies debates without replacing the documentary basis. The researcher's experience guides the selection of material, without being a criterion of proof.

With this, a disciplined hierarchy is preserved. The conceptual instruments guide the gaze and help formulate more precise questions. The sources support what can be asserted about promises, powers, procedures and effects of the observed regime. The critical literature qualifies debates, puts readings under tension and makes interpretive choices explicit, without replacing the documentary basis that supports the reconstruction.<1>p. 50</1>

Because of the researcher's insertion in the field, experience functions as a position of observation and interpretation to guide the selection and reading of the material, but not as a criterion of proof.<1>p. 49</1>
How are the chapters organized?

The reconstruction moves in three stages. It describes the regime that administers access, permanence and meaning of the digital good, stabilizes categories of qualification, proof and imputation under the CDC, made compatible with intellectual property, and tests these keys in illustrative applications. The theoretical scope is organized by functional axes, and not by authors, with technique and infrastructure, culture and communication, political economy and extraction, semiotics and platform governance.

The legal control of these ecosystems depends on a vocabulary capable of making nameable, demonstrable and imputable decisions that today hide as technical functioning. For this reason, the work is organized in linked movements, through which it describes the governance regime that administers access, permanence and meaning of the digital good, stabilizes categories of qualification, proof and imputation under the Consumer Protection Code in compatibility with the legislation on which intellectual property rights are based and, finally, tests these keys in illustrative applications with typical examples of continuous digital consumption, in which unilateral reconfigurations and platform sanctions shift what counts as delivery, alter enjoyment and redistribute losses.<1>p. 30</1>

The theoretical scope functions as a grid of observation and control designed to guide the reading of the empirical material and to discipline inferences. Instead of operating as an inventory of authors, it is organized by functional axes, each associated with research questions and reading criteria.<1>p. 53</1>

A first axis treats technique and infrastructure as a form of rationality that structures possibilities of action and interpretation. A second axis treats the cultural and communicational dimension as a condition for the formation of expectations, promises and intelligibility in interface-mediated environments, also mobilizing, in a structural key, contributions from the anthropology of consumption to describe how goods, belonging and routines stabilize meanings and coordinate conduct.<1>p. 53</1>

A third axis reconstructs political economy and extraction to situate dependencies, tolls and forms of capture associated with the operation of the ecosystem. A fourth axis describes the semiotic dimension as a material component of value and as a condition of legal cognizability of the conflict, including the notion of regimes of value and of socially administered mutability of the object over time.<1>p. 53</1>
A fifth axis reconstructs platform governance as the exercise of private power through internal rules and sanction mechanisms.<1>p. 53-54</1>
